# SIEM Telemetry Emission {.unnumbered}

## What this section covers

A SIEM can only correlate what a tenant actually emits. This section is the
**emission side** of the evidence pipeline: the portal click-paths and the
Graph / ARM / Office 365 Management API calls that turn Microsoft Entra ID,
Azure, and Microsoft 365 into compliant audit-event producers — and the
verification queries that prove they are still producing.

Everything downstream of emission already has a home in the corpus:

| Concern | Where it lives |
|---|---|
| Sentinel connectors, detection rules, UEBA, SOC playbooks | [Vol III Book 06 — SIEM & XDR Detection](../../orgcomp-series/Vol_III_Book_06_OrgComp_SIEM_XDR_Detection.qmd) |
| Canonical claim shape the ingested events normalize into | [SIEM / Audit Event Adapter spec](../../adapter-specs/siem/siem.qmd) |
| Provenance envelope and determinism contract for telemetry | [Telemetry Modernization Spec](../../modernization-specs/telemetry/telemetry.qmd) |
| Signals the FedRAMP Moderate boundary blocks outright | [Event Logging Under the GCC-Moderate Boundary](../../whitepapers/event-logging-fedramp-boundary-limitations.qmd) |

This section fills the gap between them: **nobody had written down how to
switch the emission on.**

::: {.callout-important}
## Emission is not the default

Microsoft Entra ID retains audit and sign-in logs for **7 days** on Entra ID
Free and **30 days** on P1/P2, and `MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs` are **not
retained at all** unless exported. Retention changes are **not retroactive** —
data that has aged out cannot be recovered. See
[Microsoft Entra data retention](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/monitoring-health/reference-reports-data-retention#how-long-does-microsoft-entra-id-store-the-data).

An agency that has not configured diagnostic settings is not at OMB M-21-31
EL0. It is below EL0, and every day that passes is a day of evidence it can
never produce.
:::

## The three-plane emission model

Microsoft does not have one audit pipeline. It has three, with different
control surfaces, different APIs, different retention semantics, and
different failure modes. Conflating them is the single most common reason an
agency believes it is logging something it is not.

**Plane 1 — Entra ID (tenant scope).** Identity events. Configured through
Entra diagnostic settings, which are an ARM resource
(`microsoft.aadiam/diagnosticSettings`) deployed at *tenant* scope, not
resource-group scope. This is why `az monitor diagnostic-settings create`
does not work here and operators reach for the portal instead — see
[Entra ID](01-entra-id.qmd) for the `az rest` and Bicep paths that do work.

**Plane 2 — Azure Resource Manager (subscription / resource scope).**
Control-plane and resource-plane events for Azure infrastructure. Configured
through `Microsoft.Insights/diagnosticSettings`, at subscription scope for the
activity log and per-resource for resource logs. Enforceable at scale with
Azure Policy.

**Plane 3 — Microsoft 365 unified audit log (tenant scope, separate
lifecycle).** Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, and Purview events.
Retained and governed by Microsoft Purview Audit, and read through the Office
365 Management Activity API — **not** through Entra diagnostic settings and
**not** through Microsoft Graph's `auditLogs` endpoints. Microsoft states this
separation explicitly: Entra audit and sign-in logs "are separate from the
Microsoft 365 Unified Audit Log (UAL)"
([data retention reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/monitoring-health/reference-reports-data-retention#how-long-does-microsoft-entra-id-store-the-data)).

::: {.callout-warning}
## The overlap trap

`Audit.AzureActiveDirectory` in the Management Activity API and `AuditLogs` in
Entra diagnostic settings are **not the same stream**. They overlap
substantially but neither is a superset of the other, and their retention is
governed by different systems. Agencies that enable one and assume coverage of
the other produce gapped evidence that survives internal review and fails an
assessor's sampling. Enable both; deduplicate downstream in the SIEM, not at
the source.
:::

## Configuration versus query — pick the right API

Both Microsoft Graph and the diagnostic-settings pipeline can hand you Entra
audit data, and they are not interchangeable.

| | Diagnostic settings → Log Analytics / Event Hub | Microsoft Graph `auditLogs` |
|---|---|---|
| **Purpose** | Continuous bulk streaming | Targeted query, evidence sampling |
| **Volume** | Designed for it | Microsoft: "not designed for pulling large amounts of activity data" |
| **Retention** | Whatever you configure, up to 12 years | Bounded by tenant retention (7–30 days) |
| **Latency** | ~15 min to first data | Immediate |
| **Right use** | The SIEM feed | Adapter evidence pulls, spot checks, ad-hoc investigation |

Microsoft's own guidance is that pulling large volumes through Graph "might
lead to issues with pagination and performance"
([analyze activity logs with Microsoft Graph](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/monitoring-health/howto-analyze-activity-logs-with-microsoft-graph#access-reports-using-microsoft-graph-explorer)).

The substrate consequence: the [`entra-id` adapter](../../adapter-specs/entra-id/entra-id.qmd)
reads Graph for point-in-time claims about directory *state*; the
[`siem` adapter](../../adapter-specs/siem/siem.qmd) reads the SIEM for
interval claims about *events*. Routing event evidence through Graph
collapses that distinction and breaks the `evidence-class` declaration in
the adapter registry.

## Sovereign cloud endpoints

Every API in this section has distinct endpoints per cloud. Using the
commercial endpoint against a GCC High or DoD tenant fails
authentication — access tokens are not interchangeable across clouds
([Microsoft Graph national cloud deployments](https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/deployments)).

| Surface | GCC (current UIAO boundary) | GCC High (L4) | DoD (L5) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Azure portal | `portal.azure.com` | `portal.azure.us` | `portal.azure.us` |
| Entra ID / token | `login.microsoftonline.com` | `login.microsoftonline.us` | `login.microsoftonline.us` |
| Microsoft Graph | `graph.microsoft.com` | `graph.microsoft.us` | `dod-graph.microsoft.us` |
| Management Activity API | `manage-gcc.office.com` | `manage.office365.us` | `manage.protection.apps.mil` |

::: {.callout-note}
## GCC uses the worldwide endpoints

Microsoft is explicit that a Microsoft 365 **GCC** environment continues to
use `portal.azure.com` and `graph.microsoft.com`; only **GCC High** and **DoD**
move to the `.us` endpoints
([national cloud deployments](https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/deployments#microsoft-graph-and-graph-explorer-service-root-endpoints)).
The Management Activity API is the exception — GCC has its own
`manage-gcc.office.com` endpoint
([Management Activity API troubleshooting](https://learn.microsoft.com/office/office-365-management-api/troubleshooting-the-office-365-management-activity-api#troubleshooting-the-office-365-management-activity-api)).

The current UIAO deployment boundary is GCC-Moderate per
[AGENTS.md](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/AGENTS.md), so the
worldwide column applies except where the table says otherwise.
:::

## Compliance drivers in one paragraph

**OMB M-21-31** sets the federal event-logging maturity tiers (EL0–EL3) and
the retention floor — 12 months active plus 18 months cold at EL1
([M-21-31](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/M-21-31-Improving-the-Federal-Governments-Investigative-and-Remediation-Capabilities-Related-to-Cybersecurity-Incidents.pdf)).
**NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5** supplies the control language the assessor grades
against: AU-2 (event logging), AU-3 (record content), AU-6 (review and
analysis), AU-11 (retention), AU-12 (record generation), SI-4 (system
monitoring). **CISA** contributes the SCuBA secure-configuration baselines and
the BOD directives that assume this telemetry already exists. **FedRAMP**
consumes it as the KSI-MLA indicator family — `LET` (logging event types),
`OSM` (operating SIEM capability), `RVL` (reviewing logs), `ALA` (authorizing
log access), `EVC` (evaluating configurations).

The full mapping, with the specific log categories each control depends on,
is in [Compliance crosswalk and verification](04-compliance-crosswalk.qmd).
